_purpose: Compact index of everything Meera has already published. Passed to the scoring call so it can detect repeats (novelty criterion). Keep entries short. Add a row whenever she publishes something new.

items.title: Why the niacinamide % on the label is meaningless alone
items.core_claim: Label percentage is the start of the question: pH (niacin conversion below ~4), delivery base, and batch consistency decide what you actually get.
anecdotes: Months adjusting serum base until CoA matched application tests
Brief to contract manufacturer required pH docs, 3-month stability, mid-batch CoA

items.title: The stability review meeting that started Skinstinct
items.core_claim: Industry has a gap between formulation science and marketing claims; Skinstinct exists to do documentation properly.
anecdotes: 2021 pharma meeting: 8% active at pH 3.2 with unsupportable 24-month stability claim; nobody asked; she left 7 months later

items.title: Our formulation was designed for the wrong climate
items.core_claim: Imported/foreign-validated bases fail in Indian humidity; ask what climate the base was validated for.
anecdotes: 23% returns cited texture; 71% of those from >70% humidity cities
Reformulated lighter base, humid-city returns fell to 8%

items.title: "Clinically tested" means whatever the brand wants
items.core_claim: 'Clinically tested' is unregulated in India; ask in writing for participants, design, who ran it.
anecdotes: Mumbai trade fair booth rep never answered what the testing was

items.title: What you're actually signed up for
items.core_claim: The list is formulation science, not sales; honest about gaps between labels and chemistry.
anecdotes: 2 years pharma formulation; not a dermatologist

items.title: What an active actually does
items.core_claim: An active works only if it reaches the site, at effective concentration, intact; INCI confirms none of this.
anecdotes: Vitamin C degrading near a window in Mumbai summer

items.title: pH - the question nobody puts on the label
items.core_claim: Actives have pH windows; layering mixes pH environments; brands should publish pH.
anecdotes: Customer asked if serum was compatible with her Vitamin C; serum pH 5.5-5.8

items.title: The Vitamin C email
items.core_claim: Vitamin C derivatives differ; L-ascorbic acid is hard to stabilise; many products imply its research while using derivatives.
anecdotes: 14 months trying to formulate a Vitamin C product she's satisfied with
Needed airless pump, pH<3.5, antioxidant support

items.title: Why there's no fragrance in anything we make
items.core_claim: Fragrance has the highest contact sensitisation rate and hides hundreds of compounds under one term.

items.title: The one thing I want you to stop doing with SPF
items.core_claim: People apply a quarter to half the tested SPF amount; SPF in moisturiser is not a substitute.

items.title: Ceramides and the barrier
items.core_claim: Barrier = corneocytes in a lipid matrix (~50% ceramides, 25% cholesterol, 15% FFAs); ceramide type, base and ratio matter; strip back before adding actives.
anecdotes: Skinstinct uses ceramide NP and AP with cholesterol and fatty acids

items.title: "Natural" in a formulation lab means something specific
items.core_claim: 'Natural' is unregulated; processing and sourcing documentation matter more than the label word.
anecdotes: Materials labelled cold-pressed arrived with temperature logs well above cold-press range
Squalane olive vs sugarcane; centella forms

items.title: Clean beauty gets some things right
items.core_claim: Clean beauty pushed useful scrutiny but blacklists mix real and non-risks (parabens); 'clean' is a marketing category, not a scientific one.
anecdotes: Doesn't use parabens for pragmatic/trust reasons, not because evidence says they're dangerous

items.title: Peptides: what the research actually says
items.core_claim: Peptide signalling is real but products often use sub-therapeutic concentrations; '7 peptides' is not better than 2 effective ones.
anecdotes: No peptide product sold - no commercial stake

items.title: 18 months of Skinstinct
items.core_claim: Honest retrospective: 67% 12-month repeat rate, climate mistake, communication is most of the job.
anecdotes: Explained fragrance-free choice a few hundred times
